Investor guide

Cash flow vs. appreciation: choosing a strategy

Two different reasons to own a property. Knowing which one you're buying for changes what you buy.

Ali Bayat
Figures checked against the sources below on November 21, 2026
2-minute readFor investorsGTA market, 2026

01Two strategies

Cash flow

Rent covers every cost, with money left over.

Works best when

  • You want income now
  • You can't carry a monthly shortfall
  • Multi-unit homes, larger down payments

Watch out for

  • Fewer properties qualify in the GTA
  • More management work
  • Tenant and repair risk

Appreciation

You accept a shortfall today for value growth later.

Works best when

  • Long time horizon
  • Stable income to cover shortfalls
  • Areas with transit or growth plans

Watch out for

  • Prices can fall
  • Higher rates widen the shortfall
  • Gains only show up when you sell

02Appreciation isn't guaranteed

−4.3%GTA benchmark priceMLS® HPI composite, Oct 2026 vs. Oct 2025
−2.7%GTA average priceYear over year, October 2026
2.5%Bank of Canada policy rateRaised October 28, 2026

03Questions to decide

  • How much can I top up each month?For how many years, if rates rise?
  • When might I need this money back?A short horizon favours cash flow.
  • How much work do I want?More units means more calls.
  • What's my plan if prices fall 10%?Hold, rent longer, or sell?
Ali's take

Pick one strategy per property and buy for it. The deals that go wrong are the ones bought for appreciation that the owner can't afford to hold.
